issues.description: GetLimit mutates the shared RateLimit object's Stats and FullKey per request, creating a data race
issues.detail: The override block reassigns rateLimit.Stats and rateLimit.FullKey on a *RateLimit pulled from the shared descriptor tree. Concurrent requests stomp each other's state, and sequential tests cannot witness the race. Compute Stats per-request into a local or return a fresh copy rather than mutating shared config state.

issues.description: Per-request NewStats allocation with a throwaway counter registered in the stats store
issues.detail: NewRateLimit is invoked with the stale FullKey just to be overwritten by a second NewStats call for enhancedKey. NewStats registers a counter in the store; doing this on the hot path per request both wastes the first allocation and inflates the stats store unboundedly. Compute the final key once at load and allocate stats once.

issues.description: Three near-identical key-building branches collapse to one predicate
issues.detail: The matchedViaWildcard, matchedUsingValue, and default arms all reduce to: append entry.Key, and append '_'+value when (valueToMetric || matchedUsingValue) and value is non-empty. The thirty-line switch is one rule. Collapse it; the current shape is special-cases hiding a single decision.

issues.description: Override guard compares enhancedKey against a FullKey that may never have been assigned
issues.detail: FullKey is only set in the detailed_metric branch. On non-detailed paths it is the zero value (or, given the mutation bug, residue from a prior request), so `enhancedKey != rateLimit.FullKey` is not a meaningful correctness predicate. Establish the FullKey invariant at construction or compute the key decision from data, not from a possibly-unset field.

issues.description: Metric-key construction is complected with descriptor traversal and duplicated alongside detailed_metric
issues.detail: GetLimit interleaves descriptor walking, wildcard matching, and two parallel key builders (detailedMetricFullKey, valueToMetricFullKey) with overlapping rules. Extract a per-descriptor segment renderer (e.g. metricSegment(entry, mode)) computed once at load, and drive one builder from it. This also raises the question of whether value_to_metric should generalize detailed_metric rather than parallel it.

issues.description: Positional struct literal for rateLimitDescriptor is fragile against future field additions
issues.detail: Both construction sites use positional initialization: `&rateLimitDescriptor{map{}, rateLimit, nil, descriptorConfig.ValueToMetric}`. Any added field silently shifts meanings at both call sites without a compile error if types align. Use named-field initialization to make the struct contract explicit.

synthesis.summary: The panel reaches strong consensus that the feature is reasonable but the implementation has two serious bugs and several structural issues. GetLimit mutates a shared *RateLimit from the descriptor tree per request, which is a data race the sequential tests cannot witness, and it allocates a throwaway NewStats counter every call, inflating the stats store on the hot path. The override guard `enhancedKey != rateLimit.FullKey` compares against a field that is unset on the common path. Structurally, three near-identical branches collapse to one predicate, and the new key-building logic duplicates detailed_metric inside the lookup loop. Fix by computing the metric key per-request without mutating shared state, allocating stats once, and extracting a per-descriptor segment renderer.
